definition: Superfluous means exceeding what is necessary.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word superfluous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know superfluous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: With both concerts already sold out, the third week of radio ads was superfluous.
A spare key exceeds today's need on purpose and earns its keep next month; superfluous extras exceed any need at all.
Burdensome sits past superfluous: the extra has stopped being harmless and started costing you — weight in the pack, noise in the text.

Unnecessary is the plain, everyday verdict: not needed at all, now or later, and better left out. Superfluous is more precise — the supply was right in kind but overflowed the need, like a fourth proof after three had settled the theorem. Superfluous points at the overflow; unnecessary just says no.

Excess is the amount past the required amount — the noun for the overflow itself: the third egg when the recipe asked for two. Superfluous is the judgment passed on that overflow, the adjective that says the extra serves no purpose. You measure an excess; you dismiss the superfluous.

Superfluous doesn't accuse the sign of being wrong — only of exceeding the need.
Take it down and nothing changes; that removability is the test.
The root says it plainly: super (over) + flu (flow) — the supply has overflowed the need, and the extra is running over the rim.
Superfluous measures against need: on-topic, in kind, but past the required amount — the fourth proof, the second signature line.
Extraneous, its unit-mate, measures against the subject: imported from outside it altogether.
And when the excess is specifically a repeat, this unit gives you a third tool — redundancy.
Overflow, outsider, echo: three different flaws.
